messages.copy.glossaryEntries.99cc0737fb: It is the xG sum of the shots the opponent made against us. It shows the quality and quantity of opportunities allowed by the defense.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.84fa4ea8c2: Add the xG of the opponent's shots in the same way. If the value obtained by subtracting the actual goals conceded from the expected goals conceded is positive, the goalkeeper and defense prevented the goal better than expected.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.499b32038e: If it's below 1.0 per game, it's solid defense, and if it's above 1.5, they're giving up too many chances.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.22664f2ec1: Opta's xA calculates the probability that the pass itself will be helpful based on the location and type of the pass. FBref's xAG (Expected Assists) adds the xG of the shot that led to that pass to the player who passed it.

messages.copy.glossaryEntries.718736f387: FBref (StatsBomb data) separately counts successful passes into the penalty box and carries of the ball into the box. Together they are called box entry. It's the stage right before shooting, so it shows how deep the attack went.

messages.copy.glossaryEntries.0d46a272ba: Opta·StatsBomb counts passes and carries that move the ball into the last third of the opponent's half as entries into the final third. messages.copy.glossaryEntries.5444d78f9b: Successful passes and carries that move the ball from the lower strip to the strip in front of the box (16.5 to 35 meters from the opponent's goal line) are counted. Balls moved to the side within the front strip of the box are not counted.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.c5fb4c382c: It's usually more than what enters the box. If there are a lot of entries in front of the box, but there are only a few entries in the box, it means that you are just spinning the ball in front of the opponent's block and not able to make the last shot.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.e26afa5bd8: FIFA (EFI) counts passes sent through, sideways, or above one of the opponent's lines (attack, midfield, and defense lines) as line breaks. Impect's packing counts the number of opponents defeated by such passes.

messages.copy.glossaryEntries.88671b7f6f: The team has about 1 shot per game and the success rate is about 43%. There are many teams where wingers and fullbacks penetrate all the way to the goal line.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.3a3886b0f1: Based on Opta·StatsBomb, a through pass is a pass sent to a teammate who penetrates into the space between the defense or behind the defense.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.5f4169ad80: Count attempted and successful passes to a teammate running into the back space or to a teammate standing beyond the opponent's last line of defense (the second opponent from the back). A penetration pass that is offside is also counted as a try.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.f22f15a348: The team attempts inside and outside twice per game and the success rate is about 34%. If there are many attempts, it is an attack aimed at the space behind the opponent.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.83324aaf29: FBref Definition: A carry that carries the ball more than 10 yards towards the opponent's goal or into the box.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.61b7177e2d: Count carries that drive the ball into the higher belt (horizontal area towards the opponent's goal). This also includes cases of crossing the belt with a successful dribble break.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.f1d978cf52: The team usually plays around 19 times per game. If you look at it together with the forward pass, you can tell whether the ball is mainly passed or driven.

messages.copy.glossaryEntries.f72eb6f1a4: It can be a foul if a tackle fails or the player who is driving the ball falls. Rough tackles, pressure tactics, and counterattacks are more common when breaking up counterattacks, and players who receive warnings are more careful and commit fewer offenses. messages.copy.glossaryEntries.01555e8c92: The two teams combined usually play around 22 times per game. Teams with strong pressure tend to commit more offenses.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.855a9a74e6: Referees give warnings (yellow cards) for rough fouls, tactical fouls, and protests, and send-offs (red cards) for blocking obvious scoring opportunities or serious fouls. The second yellow card in a game is an ejection.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.17cb3a77f5: Karun Singh's Expected Threat divides the playing field into squares and gives each square a probability that the team with the ball in that space will score within a few actions. If a pass or carry moves the ball to a high-threat area, it is considered to have contributed to the difference.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.2d4b938ebd: The threat level of 40 squares is the average value of the square width of the 12×8 grid published by Karun Singh (EPL 2017/18). For each successful pass and carry, the threat value of the arrival space minus the threat of the starting space is added only when the value is positive, and it is not subtracted even if the threat decreases by turning back. It is recorded in units of 1/1000 and shows up to two decimal places.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.6ab6994e1b: Khan's threat level is 0.01~0.02 in the midfield, 0.03 in front of the arc, 0.06 in the cutback area, 0.15 near the penalty spot, and 0.24 in the center of the goal area. A pass sent from the opponent's midfield to near the penalty spot adds around 0.13. Great for comparing who moved the ball into dangerous places.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.5a13f33c49: According to Opta, a cross is a pass sent from the side into the opponent's box. Success is when the ball reaches a teammate in the box, and the league average success rate is 24-28%.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.e29d71ce4c: Cross attempts sent into the box in front of the box, inside the box, or from the goal area strip are counted, as are successful shots received by a teammate or shot as a header. A ball that is caught by the goalkeeper or won by the defense is a failure. Corner kicks and side free kick deliveries also count as crosses. Please note the cutback separately.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.4db0023456: The team scores around 17 times per game, and about one out of four succeeds. If there are many attempts and the success rate is low, it may mean that there are not enough players in the box who are strong at aerial balls.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.312161e645: It is a low pass that goes close to the goal line and then pulls back inside the box (Opta's pull-back). It comes out when the defense is looking towards the goal and takes a step back, leading to a shot with a high probability of scoring.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.8e3d4f05c8: Only cuts sent to a teammate in the box from the cutback area (left and right halfspaces of the goal area strip) and received by a teammate are counted. The player who receives it shoots immediately, and the xG of that shot is 1.25 times.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.24c8b154de: Analysis media divides the stadium into vertical lanes (side, half space, center) and horizontal zones to see where the ball is handled. The lane boundary follows the line between the penalty box and the goal area (FIFA/IFAB marked line).
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.0f868c6267: The 105×68m stadium is divided into 5 lanes x 8 strips and 40 spaces based on the attack direction. The lanes are the left side, left halfspace, center, right halfspace, and right side, and the strips are from our goal line to our goal area, our box, defensive area, midfield of our camp, midfield of the opponent's camp, in front of the box, inside the box, and goal area. Usually, the space is called "lane + strip" (e.g. in front of the left halfspace box), and the area in front of the arc, near the penalty spot, cutback area, near post, far post, side next to the box, and near the corner have separate names. In the center of the goal area, half of the goal on the side where the ball is located is the near post, and the other half is the far post. Player positions, statistics, and commentary all use this column.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.a21e31075d: In the table below, the opponent's goal is at the top. If there is only a band name in the column, the lane name of that column is added in front and read. The closer the center square is to the opponent's goal, the higher the threat level (xT).

messages.copy.glossaryEntries.a5e32a8767: Analysts and commentators explain the situation at the moment of receiving the ball in terms of relative positions. Between the lines (between the opponent's midfield line and the defensive line), in the back space (behind the deepest defender), in the channels (between the centre-backs and full-backs), pressing (StatsBomb is about 4.6m of the opponent), back-to-back, numerical superiority, and phase counterattacks and gegenpressing (pressing to win the ball back immediately after losing it) (FIFA EFI, Spielverlagerung, Coaches' Voice).
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.a40f6f8b6f: The card probability is calculated for each foul. Tactical fouls that stop counterattacks often result in warnings, and fouls that prevent obvious scoring opportunities often result in expulsions. A second yellow card counts as one yellow card and one red card. The team that has been ejected runs with one less person.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.57838c3c1c: The numbers in the table indicate the order of warning and expulsion. If warnings accumulate, it may lead to suspension from the next game.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.bc5b4c58f9: Rule of the Game (IFAB): If the pass is played by a teammate in the opponent's half who is closer to the opponent's goal line than the second opponent behind the ball, it is offside. It starts again with an indirect free kick from the opposing team.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.ba23659e74: If the receiving teammate is in the opponent's half at the moment the pass goes out and is in front of the second opponent behind the ball, it is offside. Start again with an indirect free kick from the opponent. A high defensive line is better at penetrating, and attackers with good judgment are able to time their runs well.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.65b3e730ec: The average is around 4 times per game for both teams. If it gets caught a lot, it means that the opponent's defensive line is high or they are often trying to penetrate the back space.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.06ec910710: It is a situation where the ball stops and then starts again, such as a corner kick, free kick, penalty kick, or throw-in. According to Opta, set pieces excluding penalties account for 20-28% of goals, and penalties account for 7.7%.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.f2d46716db: If the last ball touched by the defense crosses the goal line, it is a corner kick. Corner kicks and side free kicks are delivered into the box to compete for aerial balls and second balls, and free kicks from shooting range are kicked directly or raised. Penalty kicks are decided by the kicker's shooting and composure and the goalkeeper's save. Corner kicks are counted towards the kicking team.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.c9699457da: The average number of corner kicks for both teams is around 10 per game. Teams that take a lot of corner kicks often push into the opponent's box.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.40a048d5c0: Every time the ball is handled, it is recalculated based on the players' positions. Between the lines: Between the average position of the opponent's midfield line and defensive line, halfspace, central lane. Empty space between the lines (pocket): Between the lines and the nearest opponent is more than 6m away. Backspace: In front of the second opponent from the back. Channel: In the halfspace, within 6 meters of the opponent's defensive line, between their centre-back and full-back. Pressure: Number of opponents within 4.6 meters (1 for opponents near goal, 0.5 for opponents behind the goal). Receiving with your back: You receive a pass from behind, but there is an opponent within 3m of the goal. Numerical superiority: There are more players than the opponent within 15m around the ball. Counterattack: Within 8 seconds of getting the ball back, there are 5 or fewer opponents on goal than the ball. Gegenpressing: Pressing radius increases depending on tactics for 5 seconds after losing the ball.
messages.copy.glossaryEntries.daffa517b8: If “received between the lines”, “received in the back space”, “received with your back turned”, or “counterattack” appears in the commentary, this is the tag. If the pressure is above 1, the passing success rate decreases and dribble penetration or clearance increases.
